classification.difficultyReason: Use the prescribed root relationships to form simultaneous equations, resolve two product cases and find all four zeroes.

content.prompt: Find the zeroes of $x^4-3x^3-8x^2+12x+16$ if they are $\alpha$, $2\alpha$, $\beta$, and $2\beta$.

answer.worked:
Sum of roots:
$$\begin{align*}3\alpha+3\beta&=3\\\alpha+\beta&=1\end{align*}$$
Product of roots:
$$\begin{align*}4\alpha^2\beta^2&=16\\\alpha^2\beta^2&=4\end{align*}$$
Solving simultaneously:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha^2(1-\alpha)^2&=4\\\alpha(1-\alpha)&=\pm2\end{align*}$$
Consider two cases.

For $\alpha(1-\alpha)=2$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha^2-\alpha+2&=0\\\Delta&=1-8\\&=-7<0\end{align*}$$
This case has no real solution. It also fails the quartic's coefficients: here $\alpha\beta=2$, so the sum of pairwise products would be
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha^2+9\alpha\beta+2\beta^2&=2(\alpha+\beta)^2+5\alpha\beta\\&=2(1)^2+5(2)\\&=12,\end{align*}$$
whereas the coefficient of $x^2$ requires $-8$.

For $\alpha(1-\alpha)=-2$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha^2-\alpha-2&=0\\(\alpha+1)(\alpha-2)&=0\\\alpha&=-1\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
If $\alpha=-1$, then $\beta=2$. If $\alpha=2$, then $\beta=-1$; these give the same four zeroes.

The zeroes are $-1,-2,2,4$.

Check:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)(x+2)(x-2)(x-4)&=(x^2-x-2)(x^2-2x-8)\\&=x^4-3x^3-8x^2+12x+16.\end{align*}$$
